Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and sharp detective known as a 'truth-seeker' or satyanweshi, who solves mysteries with logical reasoning alongside his friend Ajit.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the stories and often assists in investigations.

Satyawati.description: Byomkesh's wife, known for her strong opinions and spirited debates, especially regarding gender roles.

Chintamani Kundu.description: A paralyzed, elderly landlord who becomes embroiled in a murder case involving his tenant and seeks Byomkesh's help.

Ramadhin.description: Chintamani Kundu's loyal Hindustani servant who assists him in daily tasks.

Bijoy Bhaduri.description: A senior police inspector and former junior inspector known to Byomkesh who investigates the murder case.

Bidhu Bhushan Aich.description: The murder victim, a police officer from Burdwan who recognizes Pramila Pal in disguise.

Pramila Pal.description: A fugitive woman and master of disguise, previously convicted of murder, who assumes the identity of a young man named Tapan Sen.

Jamadar.description: A police officer who assists Bijoy Babu in arresting Pramila Pal.

Calcutta.description: The city (now Kolkata) where the story is set, a major metropolis in eastern India.

Kashipur.description: A locality in Calcutta mentioned as the site of a recent burglary.

Bankim Chandra.description: Refers to Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, a renowned Bengali novelist and author of 'Devi Chaudhurani'.

Devi Chaudhurani.description: A famous fictional female bandit and freedom fighter from Bankim Chandra's novel, cited as an example of a strong woman.

Burdwan.description: A city in West Bengal, India, referenced as the home of Bidhu Bhushan Aich and the location of a jail.

Chetla.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta, mentioned as the location of the girls' school where Shanta claims to work.

Madrasi.description: A term used to refer to people from the southern Indian region of Madras (now Chennai), here describing a tenant family.

Prabhat.description: Likely refers to a publishing house or a person to whom Byomkesh sends unsolicited manuscripts.

dewan.description: A type of low, backless couch or divan commonly used in Indian households.

namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, performed with folded hands.

babu.description: A term of respect or endearment for a man, often used for educated or respectable gentlemen.
